next_question: Can a session_invalidation behavioral measurement that includes /session/status probing produce within-condition variance (std>0) on all co-occurring conditions, enabling a valid pooled Pearson r test of behavioral-structural orthogonality on the fixed co-occurring drift+noise design?
why_next: This experiment fixed the parent's zero-imputation confound (unauthenticated /schema achieves 99.2% both>0) and achieved directionally low pooled r=0.0498 (12x lower than parent 0.593), but the measurement is MEASUREMENT_INVALID because session_invalidation produces constant behavioral signal (API endpoints ignore session validity). The minimum fix is to add /session/status probing to the behavioral composite for session_invalidation conditions, or to restrict the confirmatory test to permission_boundary conditions only (n=120, r=0.051, p=0.577 — directionally consistent with orthogonality but underpowered). Either fix enables a valid orthogonality test. If |r|<0.3 survives with proper measurement, C-FRESHNESS gains a validated second detection channel (behavioral signals as independent channel alongside structural). If r≥0.3 with proper measurement, the domain pivots to composite multi-signal classifiers.

established: Behavioral signals (token validation failure rate, session state change, auth boundary shift) measured from real HTTP on Flask 3.x + PyJWT HS256 localhost detect all 5 auth-drift patterns with TP=1.0 (Wilson lower 0.886) and tolerate all 4 structural noise patterns with FP=0.0. AUC=1.0 for drift-vs-noise discrimination. This is the first signal family to pass C1/C2/C3 for C-FRESHNESS (parent EXP-GRAPH-35166507358, audit PASS).

Unauthenticated /schema endpoint provides structural observability independent of auth state: 99.2% of co-occurring samples have both behavioral>0 AND structural>0, fixing parent zero-imputation confound where signing_key_rotation masked structural signal to 0.0.

Pooled Pearson r=0.0498 (|r|=0.0498) on 240 paired samples is 12x lower than parent r=0.593, directionally consistent with orthogonality. Permission_boundary-only pooled r=0.051 (n=120, p=0.577) provides cleaner estimate with proper within-condition variation.
Null control FP=0.0 on 120 noise-only samples confirms behavioral signals do not false-positive on structural noise without drift.

Six structural/schema-based signal families remain falsified for C-FRESHNESS frozen gate in deterministic mock: Jaccard, TF-IDF, response-time KS, linear Fisher LDA ensemble, field-usage profiling, direct schema comparison.
The magnitude confound is structural: unbounded optional_field_addition noise scales diff magnitude with schema size, dominating subtle drift at all sizes.

recommended_action: Redesign session_invalidation behavioral measurement to produce within-condition variance: either (a) add /session/status probing to behavioral composite with stochastic session TTL/jitter so session_state_changes varies per-sample, or (b) make API middleware check session store so auth_boundary_shifts or token_validation_failures vary. Then re-run the co-occurring drift+noise orthogonality test with ≥6/8 conditions passing the variance gate. Alternatively, if the session_invalidation fix is intractable, restrict the confirmatory pooled test to permission_boundary conditions only (n=120) with wider stochastic variation (all 7 non-empty permission subsets, n≥60 per condition) and preregister per-drift stratification. If |r|<0.3 survives with proper measurement, C-FRESHNESS gains a validated second detection channel. If r≥0.3, the domain pivots to composite multi-signal classifiers or real-API stochastic deployments.
